svg.title: Twelve months ago a public health nurse started a falls-prevention program at a 200-resident senior housing site: a weekly balance class, a medication review, and home hazard checks. In the year before the program there were 48 falls and 11 residents attended any activity. This year there were 27 falls and 96 residents attended at least one class.
svg.desc: Falls are the outcome the program exists to change, so the fall count is the outcome measure, and 48 down to 27 is a drop of about 44%. Attendance is a process measure: it shows the program was delivered and used, not that it worked, which makes it the tempting choice. Satisfaction is the weakest evidence of the three, because people can enjoy a class that changes nothing.
